title: The second identity in Kaleyski's Conjecture 21
summary: For even-dimensional APN monomials, determine whether the second distinguished DDT sum agrees with the cubic Gold-function benchmark.

formal_statement.body: Let $K=\mathbb F_{2^n}$ with even $n\ge4$, let $F_d(x)=x^d$ be APN, and write $\operatorname{DDT}_F(a,b)=|\{x\in K:F(x+a)+F(x)=b\}|$. Define $S_2(d)=\sum_{y\in K}\operatorname{DDT}_{F_d}(y+1,F_d(y))$ and $B_n=\sum_{y\in K}\operatorname{DDT}_{x^3}(y,y^3+1)$. Determine whether $S_2(d)=B_n$.

scope.domain: APN power functions and difference distribution tables
scope.unresolved_remainder: The first identity in Conjecture 21 is a separate open statement and is not included in this record.

progress.summary: Kaleyski states two DDT-sum identities for APN power functions, including the second identity recorded here.
The odd-dimensional identities were treated in later work; the even-dimensional second identity remains separately tracked here.
